added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite and no after_suite (classification.json records both as null), and its only gate log, gate-after.log, is the after arm cut at 75 of 104 collected tests with EXIT=124; with no base arm there is no measured delta, so the count is recorded as unmeasured rather than as zero.

findings.text: blocking: done-when (3) is unmet — scan-282.log departs 3 roots to 1 at 0.1735 and scan-550.log at 0.1225, and the vanished roots there carry determinants 4.5134e-05, -4.0807e-05 and 6.7124e-05 with one eigenvalue pair of opposite sign, so the census still loses a hyperbolic saddle inside both windows the done-when names, as the manifest itself reports.

blocking: done-when (4) is unmeasured — the only gate arm is cut by the node's own 480-second wall bound at 75 of 104 collected tests (EXIT=124), no base arm exists, and the manifest stores no baseline_suite/after_suite, so "pass by delta against a recorded baseline" is asserted by nothing; the structural argument that no test imports read_robustness shows no test can fail, which is not the same as a measured delta.

blocking: the only falsification the node landed returns 1 while the repair holds and 0 once the reinstated step is restored, and nothing asserts on that exit code — no test drives it and no test under tests/ imports the census — so done-when (5)'s read-level tie-state test is unwritten and a regression of the admission bound would be caught by no gate.

follow-on: done-when (2) asks for kernel.py's unused psi_rounding_enclosure to be used if it fits or deleted, and it is neither — census.py:77 leaves it in place with a prose justification, a deviation from an exact spec that was not repaired.

follow-on: the section's id is written with doubled quotes and parses to an empty string (verified with html.parser), so the section recording the round-two control and disposition has no anchor and 43bb48a70, whose stated purpose was to give that element its own id, did not achieve it.

follow-on: the gate receipt is abridged, a bare "..." line standing in for the remainder of the run and its pytest summary, and its header names neither the revision nor the tree, so the 75-of-104 claim cannot be checked from the log it is quoted from.
